# Default moulded depth: the rule against the Reference Vessels

Moulded depth is keel to main deck at the side. When an Option leaves it out, it is the depth-to-beam ratio of the Cargo times the beam, to the millimetre (`depth_to_beam_ratio` in the Defaults Profile, which a copy may edit). A Cargo is in the dry-bulk group if its phase is dry bulk, and in the gas group if it is a liquefied gas (LNG, ethane, the LPGs). Container shares the dry-bulk ratio; the liquid group has no Cargo yet.

| Group | Ratio D/B | Vessels | D/B range, all | Inland vessels | D/B range, inland |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dry bulk, container | 0.33 | 26 | 0.22 to 0.66 | 20 | 0.22 to 0.49 |
| liquid | 0.3 | 5 | 0.33 to 0.57 | 2 | 0.33 to 0.38 |
| gas | 0.55 | 8 | 0.44 to 0.66 | 1 | 0.50 to 0.50 |

The ranges are those of the vessels below, grouped by the rule in the header of `tools/gen_depth_rule.py`; the ratios are the Defaults Profile's. 41 Reference Vessels have a published depth; 2 carry no cargo (a tug or pusher), so the rule does not apply to them. A **slender** mark: the published length over depth is above 25, the soft limit.
